div.div: فَنِيقٌ A stallion, (S, O, K,) [i. e.] a stallioncamel, (IAar, TA,) that is highly regarded, (S, O, K,) and is not molested, because of the high estimation in which he is held by his owner, or owners, nor is ridden: (O, K:) it is said by AZ to be one of the names for such a stallion: (S, TA:) or it is an epithet applied to a camel, meaning such as is acquired for covering: (TA:) the pl. is فُنُقٌ (S, O, K) accord. to AZ, and أَفْنَاقٌ accord. to IDrd, (S,) or the latter is pl. of the former pl.: (O, K:) and ↓ فُنُق is applied as an epithet to a [single] camel, like فَنِيقٌ. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
